Hi Priya — great speaking earlier. Quick recap and a couple of asks so my team can put together a clean estimate:

Call recap / confirmed asks:
- Primary use: in-product conversational assistant (customer support + routing) and a light personalization layer.
- Expected steady-state token volume: ~40M tokens/month (with occasional peak months up to ~120M).
- Concurrency: rough peak ~8 concurrent user sessions for the assistant.
- Residency: you mentioned preference for EU data residency due to GDPR; also asked about implications on pricing.
- Procurement: likely 12-month commitment if terms look reasonable.

What I need from you to finalize an estimate:
1) Confirm the ballpark monthly token volume (steady and peak).
2) Confirm preferred region for data residency (EU vs US).
3) Any target $/1M tokens you had in mind for Redwood to hit under a committed contract?

Ballpark note: from experience, EU-hosted workloads typically carry a modest premium (~10–15%) vs US due to regional capacity and egress. We also commonly surface savings via prefix/KV caching and reserved capacity which can materially lower your effective $/1M. I will prepare a simple cost model and attach an initial worksheet.

Next steps:
- If you confirm volume and residency, I’ll send a formal estimate and run a quick committed capacity vs hosted pricing comparison.
- If procurement/legal needs an MSA/PO timeline, share the contact and we’ll loop in our contracts team.

Thanks — speaking to Marissa to include dedicated/reserved options if you want an SLA-backed price.

Best,

Subject: Re: FinTechCo - follow-up: pricing & regional residency (post-demo)

Thanks — appreciate the clarity. Below is a transparent, high-level ballpark to help internal discussions. I’ll attach a simple worksheet with the line items.

Assumptions: steady 40M tokens/month, peak handled with autoscaling/burst.

Ballpark unit economics (hosted API, committed 12-month term):
- US region (hosted): $45 per 1M tokens (tiered discounts possible as volume increases).
- EU region (hosted, GDPR residency): ~12% premium -> $50.40 per 1M tokens.

Illustrative monthly costs (steady 40M):
- US hosted: 40 * $45 = $1,800/month.
- EU hosted: 40 * $50.40 = $2,016/month.

Notes and levers to reduce effective $/1M:
- Prefix / KV caching: depending on your reuse patterns, effective billed tokens can drop 20–40%. We can model this if you share sample prompts or traffic shape.
- Reserved/dedicated capacity: for predictable throughput and lower latency, Dedicated commitment can lower unit price further (we typically see an additional 10–25% reduction depending on capacity sizing and guaranteed commit).
- Quantization / model selection: swapping to a slightly smaller model variant for lower-cost paths can save materially for high token volumes with minimal quality impact for many prompts.
- Data residency costs: EU residency impact includes slightly higher infra and storage costs and potentially egress; we bake that into the regional premium above. If you need on-prem VPC or Private deployment, that will change the licensing/one-time fees.

Next steps I’ll take:
1) Attach a short pricing worksheet (same folder link included below) with US vs EU line items + an option for dedicated reserved pricing.
2) Loop in contracts/CS for MSA/PO path once we confirm the target model and residency.
3) If you share a sample week of traffic or a small prompt set, we’ll run a quick caching estimate to show potential savings.

Attaching: redwood-pricing-estimate-20261018.xlsx (ballpark worksheet). Also linking HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/FT-4821

Would you and Carlos be available for a 30-minute follow-up next week to review the committed vs hosted tradeoffs?

Thanks,
Dylan
